Term: A. SYMPTOMS & EXPERIENCES (Unaware funnel - entry from search)

Definition (short): Cluster of physical + mood symptoms in the 7-10 days before period. ~75% prevalence to some degree.

Translation (Vi): Rối loạn khí sắc tiền kinh nguyệt
Definition (short): Severe form of PMS (3-8% prevalence). Clinical diagnosis. Mood disturbance significant enough to impair daily life.
Subjective cognitive cloudiness during late luteal + early menstrual. Modest measurable effects on working memory.

Translation (Vi): Tụt năng lượng theo chu kỳ
Definition (short): Predictable drop in energy correlated with phase transitions. Most pronounced late luteal + early menstrual.
Increased appetite + cravings (carbs/chocolate) in late luteal. Linked to serotonin + insulin fluctuation.
Fluid retention in late luteal phase from progesterone-driven sodium retention.

Translation (Vi): Thay đổi tâm trạng theo chu kỳ
Definition (short): Recurring mood pattern tied to phase. Predictable timing is diagnostic clue vs clinical mood disorder.
Acne pattern correlated with cycle (peaks late luteal). Driven by androgen + sebum interaction.
One-sided pelvic pain at ovulation. Usually harmless and brief (hours to 1 day).

Translation (Vi): Đau tức ngực theo chu kỳ
Definition (short): Tender swollen breasts in late luteal. Progesterone-driven; resolves with period onset.
Painful periods - primary (intrinsic) or secondary (from condition like endometriosis).
Migraine pattern timed to estrogen drop pre-period. Affects ~20% of women with migraines.
Depressive symptoms timed to luteal phase. Distinct from major depressive disorder by timing.
Anxiety spikes in late luteal - linked to allopregnanolone withdrawal + GABA dysregulation.
Periods >7 days OR soaking through pad/tampon every 1-2 hours. Warrants medical evaluation.
Periods <3 days OR very light flow. Can indicate hormonal imbalance; under-fueling; thyroid issues.
Light bleeding around ovulation. Usually harmless; persistent or heavy warrants evaluation.
Coagulated blood passed during heavy flow. Small clots normal; quarter-sized+ warrants evaluation.
Sleep disruption in late luteal + ovulatory phases from progesterone + temp shifts.
Increased frustration tolerance dropping in late luteal. Serotonin withdrawal model.
Digestive symptoms (cramping; diarrhea; constipation) worsening pre-period - prostaglandin-mediated.
Seizure pattern correlated with cycle phases. Affects ~40% of women with epilepsy.
Recurring hormonal cycle from day 1 of menstruation to day before next period. Normal: 21-35 days.
Days from period start to next period start. ~12% of women have exactly 28-day cycles.
One of 4 cycle segments: menstrual; follicular; ovulatory; luteal. Each has distinct hormone profile.
Release of mature egg from ovary - triggered by LH surge ~24-36h prior.
Shedding of uterine lining when no implantation. Lasts 3-7 days for most. Day 1 = new cycle.
Cycle without ovulation. Common in adolescence; perimenopause; PCOS; high stress; hormonal BC.
Uterine lining that thickens through cycle responding to estrogen + progesterone. Sheds at menstruation.
Hormone-producing structure formed from follicle post-ovulation. Produces progesterone during luteal.
Fluid-filled sac in ovary containing developing egg. ~15-20 develop per cycle; one becomes dominant.
Number of viable eggs remaining. Declines with age; rapid decline starts ~age 35.
First menstrual period. Average age 12 globally; range 8-15 considered normal.
Permanent end of menstruation. Diagnosed retrospectively after 12 months without period. Average age 51.
Stage after 12 months without period. Cycle syncing no longer applies; rhythms still matter.
Hormone-producing glands. Pituitary + ovaries + thyroid + adrenals all interact with cycle.
Feedback loop controlling cycle: hypothalamus releases GnRH → pituitary releases FSH/LH → ovaries produce estrogen/progesterone.
Cohort of follicles developing each cycle (~15-20). 1 becomes dominant; rest regress.
Late follicular days (~5 days before ovulation). Peak estrogen window.
Synonym for luteal phase. Period from ovulation to next menstruation.
Primary female sex hormone (form: estradiol). Peaks late follicular + ovulatory. Supports BDNF; dopamine; serotonin.
Dominant hormone of luteal phase. Calming; sleep-promoting; raises body temp ~0.5°F after ovulation.
Present in women at ~10% male levels. Peaks ovulatory. Affects libido + assertiveness + muscle.
Stimulates follicle growth in early follicular phase. Released by pituitary.
Triggers ovulation when surging mid-cycle. Released by pituitary.
Sudden 5-10x rise in LH ~24-36h before ovulation. Detected by OPKs.
Stress hormone. Chronic elevation suppresses reproductive hormones + causes cycle irregularity.
Milk production hormone. High levels suppress ovulation (lactational amenorrhea + stress amenorrhea).

Translation (Vi): Hormone tuyến giáp và chu kỳ
Definition (short): T3/T4 levels affect cycle regularity. Hypo or hyperthyroidism commonly cause cycle disruption.
Adrenal androgen precursor. Declines with age. Some research interest in supplementation for ovarian aging.
Group including testosterone + DHEA. Elevated in PCOS; cause acne + hirsutism + cycle irregularity.
Liver-produced protein that binds sex hormones. High SHBG = low free hormone activity.
Insulin sensitivity varies across cycle - drops in luteal phase. Contributes to PMS cravings.
Relative excess of estrogen vs progesterone. Linked to heavy periods + breast tenderness + fibroids.
Inadequate progesterone production in luteal phase. Associated with short luteal phase + early miscarriage.
Plant compounds (soy isoflavones; flax lignans) with weak estrogenic activity.
Synthetic chemicals (BPA; phthalates; parabens) mimicking estrogen. Endocrine disruptors.
Estrogen + progestin therapy for perimenopause/menopause symptoms. Different from birth control.

Translation (Vi): BDNF (Yếu tố thần kinh từ não)
Definition (short): Protein supporting neuron growth + plasticity. Estrogen upregulates BDNF → follicular learning advantage.
Reward + motivation neurotransmitter. Estrogen amplifies dopamine - drives follicular novelty-seeking.
Mood + sleep neurotransmitter. Drops in late luteal - underlies PMS mood symptoms.
Inhibitory neurotransmitter; calming. Boosted by allopregnanolone in luteal phase.
Progesterone metabolite modulating GABA. Drops sharply in late luteal - contributes to PMDD.
Biological rhythm longer than 24h. Menstrual cycle is the primary female infradian rhythm.
~24-hour rhythm. Interacts with infradian; sleep architecture shifts across cycle.
Mechanism by which sex hormones affect cognitive performance (verbal fluency; working memory).

Translation (Vi): Tính dẻo thần kinh và chu kỳ
Definition (short): Brain's adaptive capacity - modulated by estrogen + BDNF cycling. Highest in late follicular.

Translation (Vi): Cấu trúc giấc ngủ và chu kỳ
Definition (short): REM + deep sleep proportions shift with cycle. Progesterone disrupts REM in late luteal.
Autonomic balance marker. Drops in luteal phase as progesterone reduces parasympathetic tone.

Translation (Vi): Điều hòa nhiệt độ cơ thể
Definition (short): Basal body temp rises ~0.5°F after ovulation. Used to confirm ovulation retrospectively.
Inflammatory markers cycle - rise in late luteal + menstrual. Drives PMS + period pain.

Translation (Vi): Độ nhạy insulin và chu kỳ
Definition (short): Insulin sensitivity highest in follicular; drops in luteal. Affects energy + cravings + training response.
Day 1 to ovulation (10-16 days). FSH + rising estrogen. Energy + creativity rise in late follicular.
Days 6-13. Peak estrogen window. Best for learning + strength training.
Days 14-16. Peak estrogen + LH surge. Verbal fluency + social ease peak here.
5 days before + day of ovulation. Sperm survive ~5 days in fertile cervical mucus.
Ovulation to next period (~14 days). Progesterone dominant. Detail orientation + completion focus.
Days 17-22. Peak detail-orientation. Best for editing; QA; closing tasks.
Days 23-28. Serotonin + allopregnanolone drop. PMS peaks. Reduce demands.
Days 1-5 (bleeding). All hormones low. Reflection + planning phase.
The 1-2 day window between phases. Symptoms often most noticeable here.
Visual representation of 4 phases on a calendar with hormone overlay. Lumen's visual primitive.
Practice of aligning lifestyle (work; exercise; diet) with 4 hormonal phases. Coined by Alisa Vitti (FloLiving).
Scheduling tasks based on predicted phase rather than calendar week. Core Lumen positioning.
Productivity framework using cycle phase as input for work mode. Distinct from period tracking.

Translation (Vi): Xoay vòng chế độ làm việc
Definition (short): Mapping 4 work modes (Reflect; Build; Connect; Finish) onto 4 cycle phases.
Day 1 of current period - reference point for predicting all 4 phases.
Updating phase predictions on day 1 of new period. Necessary because cycles drift.
Adjusting workout intensity + type by phase. Evidence mixed - 2024 meta-analysis found small effects.
Eating different foods per phase. Most overclaimed corner of cycle syncing - evidence is mostly mechanistic.
Adjusting bedtime + caffeine cutoff by phase. Late luteal needs earlier wind-down.
Adjusting skincare by phase. Wellness-coded; minimal evidence.
Eating specific seeds (flax/pumpkin in follicular; sesame/sunflower in luteal). Evidence is anecdotal only.
Scheduling cognitively demanding work in late follicular. Lumen positioning.
Reserving detail-oriented editing for early luteal phase. Higher error detection sensitivity.
Recording cycle data (period; symptoms; basal temp) for prediction.
App logging period + symptoms. Distinct from cycle syncing app (prescribes actions).
Recording subjective symptoms (energy; mood; cramps) daily to detect patterns.

Translation (Vi): Nhiệt độ cơ thể cơ bản
Definition (short): Lowest body temp at rest. Rises ~0.5°F post-ovulation. Confirms ovulation retrospectively.
Specialized thermometer (0.01°F precision) for tracking BBT.
Observing cervical mucus texture changes. Egg-white consistency = fertile window.

Translation (Vi): Phương pháp nhận biết khả năng sinh sản
Definition (short): Birth control method combining BBT + cervical mucus + cycle tracking.
FAM variant combining BBT + cervical mucus + symptoms. Highest-efficacy FAM.
Calendar-based FAM. Avoid intercourse days 8-19. Lower efficacy than sympto-thermal.
Predicting ovulation purely from cycle calendar. Least reliable FAM variant.

Translation (Vi): Phương pháp vô kinh do cho con bú
Definition (short): Using exclusive breastfeeding as birth control (first 6 months). Up to 98% effective if strict criteria met.
Urine test detecting LH surge. Predicts ovulation 24-36h ahead.

Translation (Vi): Thiết bị đeo theo dõi chu kỳ
Definition (short): Wearable (Oura; Whoop; Apple Watch) tracking BBT + HRV + heart rate to predict phases.

Translation (Vi): Máy theo dõi sinh sản liên tục
Definition (short): Devices (Mira; Inito) measuring hormone metabolites in urine continuously.
Tool converting last period date + cycle length into 4 phase date ranges. Lumen's core product.
Ability to download cycle history. Important for privacy + provider sharing. Varies by app.

Translation (Vi): Theo dõi chu kỳ bảo mật
Definition (short): Tracking with local-only data + no account + no third-party sharing. Increasingly important post-Roe.

Translation (Vi): PCOS (Hội chứng buồng trứng đa nang)
Definition (short): Endocrine disorder affecting 8-13% of women. Irregular ovulation + androgen excess. Disrupts cycle syncing.
Endometrial-like tissue grows outside uterus. Severe period pain + can impact cycle regularity.

Translation (Vi): Lạc nội mạc tử cung trong cơ
Definition (short): Endometrial tissue grows into uterine muscle wall. Heavy painful periods.
Non-cancerous growths in uterine wall. Common in 30s-40s. Can cause heavy bleeding.
Hormonal transition before menopause (late 30s to 50s). Follicular phase shortens first.

Translation (Vi): Chu kỳ trở lại sau sinh
Definition (short): First cycles after childbirth - often anovulatory + irregular. Predictions unreliable 3-6 cycles.

Translation (Vi): Vô kinh do cho con bú
Definition (short): Ovulation suppression during exclusive breastfeeding. Cycles may not return for months to >1 year.
Cycle loss from under-fueling; over-training; chronic stress. Reversible. Common in athletes.
Loss of ovarian function before age 40. Affects ~1% of women.

Translation (Vi): RED-S (Thiếu năng lượng tương đối ở vận động viên)
Definition (short): Cluster: low energy availability + menstrual dysfunction + low bone density. Affects ~30% of female athletes.

Translation (Vi): Vô kinh chức năng vùng hạ đồi
Definition (short): Reversible cycle loss from stress/under-fueling. Treated by addressing root cause not by adding hormones.
Delayed cycle return after stopping hormonal birth control. Most resolve within 3 months.
Estrogen + progestin (pill; patch; ring). Suppresses ovulation. Cycle syncing not applicable.
Progestin without estrogen. Variable ovulation suppression. Cycle syncing may partially apply.
Levonorgestrel-releasing IUD (Mirena; Kyleena; Liletta). Often suppresses ovulation.
Non-hormonal IUD (Paragard). Does NOT suppress cycle. Cycle syncing applies normally.
Etonogestrel implant. Suppresses ovulation in most users. Cycle syncing not applicable.
Medroxyprogesterone injection every 3 months. Suppresses ovulation. Slow cycle return after stopping.
Combined hormonal ring. Same hormonal effect as combined pill.
Combined hormonal patch. Same hormonal effect as combined pill.
Scheduled bleed during placebo week of combined pill. Not a true period.
Post-coital contraceptive. Levonorgestrel (Plan B) or ulipristal (Ella). Effective up to 72-120h.
Transition back to natural cycle. May involve irregular cycles for 3-6 months.

Term: J. CYCLE SYNCING ON CONSTRAINTS (Converting practice)

Translation (Vi): Cycle syncing khi dùng thuốc tránh thai
Definition (short): Most hormonal methods suppress cycling; non-hormonal preserve it. Method-by-method nuance.
Modified approach for irregular cycles: track ovulation directly (OPK; BBT) rather than calendar predict.

Translation (Vi): Cycle syncing trong tiền mãn kinh
Definition (short): Track shortening cycles + symptoms over months. Calendar predictions become unreliable.

Translation (Vi): Cycle syncing cho lạc nội mạc tử cung
Definition (short): Severe period pain disrupts standard menstrual phase recommendations. Pain management priority.

Translation (Vi): Cycle syncing cho vận động viên
Definition (short): Training periodization aligned to cycle. Stacy Sims framework; evidence mixed but practical.
Mineral with moderate evidence for reducing PMS symptoms. Typical dose 200-400mg/day glycinate form.
Cofactor for serotonin synthesis. Evidence for moderate PMS reduction. Dose: 50-100mg/day.
Lost during menstruation. Heavy bleeders often iron-deficient. Test ferritin before supplementing.
EPA/DHA reduce inflammatory PMS symptoms. Dose: 1-2g combined EPA/DHA daily.
Herbal extract with moderate evidence for cycle regularity + PMS. Affects prolactin + dopamine.
Myo + D-chiro inositol show evidence for improving ovulation + insulin sensitivity in PCOS.
Anti-androgenic effects in small studies. Used for hirsutism in PCOS.
Cycle syncing popularizer; FloLiving founder; author of "WomanCode" + "In the FLO".
Female athlete physiology researcher; author of "ROAR". Cycle-aware training research.
Naturopathic doctor; author of "Period Repair Manual". Evidence-based women's health.
Influential review of cognitive variation across menstrual cycle. Used to ground evidence claims.
Meta-analysis finding small effect of phase-timed exercise on training outcomes. Cooled hype.

Topic: Edge cases + birth control + practice variations
